text:
Pavel Buchnevich missed Wednesday's game in New York with an upper-body injury, and the Blues won anyway. Then he came back Friday against Dallas and set up two goals in another win. That makes a five-game point streak (three goals, three assists) for a 31-year-old who has quietly become steady again on a St. Louis team that has won seven of its last eight he's played.

Nothing about his scoring looks borrowed. Six goals on 5.9 expected is dead on his chances, and the Blues control a bit more of the play with him on the ice than without him. The one soft spot: St. Louis has been finishing better than expected around him (about 5.5 goals above the chances), which flatters his assists.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags a habit worth watching: 19% of his setups come from behind the net, more than twice a typical forward. Our range puts his season between 37 and 55 points, about where his career has lived. Watch the upper body, and the streak.
